record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Does there exist a non-rational exotic C^n?

evidence.quote: 2.7. PROBLEM. Does there exist a non-rational exotic Cn ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a smooth complex affine algebraic variety $X$ of dimension $n$ an exotic $\mathbb{C}^n$ if $X$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ (equivalently, $X$ is contractible and, for $n\ge 3$, has the underlying smooth manifold structure of $\mathbb{C}^n$) but $X$ is not isomorphic, as an algebraic variety, to the affine space $\mathbb{C}^n$. Recall that $X$ is rational if its function field $\mathbb{C}(X)$ is purely transcendental over $\mathbb{C}$, i.e. isomorphic to $\mathbb{C}(t_1,\dots,t_n)$.

Question: Does there exist an integer $n\ge 1$ and an exotic $\mathbb{C}^n$ that is not rational?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches on exotic structures on $\mathbb{C}^n$, rationality of contractible smooth affine varieties, and related work of Zaidenberg, Kaliman, and others did not surface a published resolution of this specific question. Known constructions of exotic $\mathbb{C}^n$ (e.g., Ramanujam-type surfaces crossed with affine lines, tom Dieck–Petrie examples) typically yield rational varieties, but no explicit non-rational example or proof of non-existence appears to be recorded. Status appears to be unknown/open based on available sources.

status_evidence.title: Challenging problems on affine n-space (Kraft)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of problems concerning affine n-space, including exotic structures and rationality questions for contractible affine varieties.
status_evidence.claim: The question of whether non-rational exotic affine spaces exist is discussed among open problems on affine n-space without resolution.

status_evidence.title: The Zariski Cancellation Problem and related problems in affine algebraic geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Recent survey covering exotic affine spaces, contractible affine varieties and cancellation; standard examples of exotic C^n are rational.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys of exotic affine spaces do not record a non-rational example, suggesting the problem remains open.
